facts.text: There were no capacity errors on the nights of 2030-04-01 and 2030-04-02; m8g.24xlarge InsufficientInstanceCapacity errors start on the night of 2030-04-03 and continue every night after, in both AZs.

The errors started right after both m8g.24xlarge capacity reservations (100 instances each, eu-west-1a and eu-west-1b) were cancelled with CancelCapacityReservation on 2030-04-03 around 10:00 UTC. Without reservations the shared pool cannot cover the peak.
Gives correct sizes for the problem: per night about 45 failed m8g.24xlarge in eu-west-1a and about 35 in eu-west-1b (180 and 140 in total over the 4 nights from 2030-04-03).
The m8g.16xlarge fallback launched successfully (no errors); this is not a quota problem.

Now: re-create or keep (part of) the reservations for the peak, possibly in batches, and rely on the 16xlarge fallback meanwhile. Next time: agree a rollback condition / check peak capacity BEFORE releasing reservations. Names owners (customer platform team, AWS account team / TAM).

wrong_claims.text: Suggests a quota increase as the fix.
Says the cause is unknown or random, or does not connect the errors to the cancelled reservations.
Recommends pausing or rolling back the Graviton rollout as the main answer.
Reports failure counts inflated by duplicate records.
